title: Caused, Yet Free?
paragraphs: Few philosophical questions feel as personal as whether we choose freely. If every event, including every thought, follows from earlier causes according to natural laws, it seems to follow that our decisions were fixed long before we made them. Those who accept this conclusion and deny that we are free are sometimes called free will sceptics; those who insist that we are free precisely because our choices escape such necessity are known, somewhat confusingly, as libertarians.

A third camp, compatibilism, rejects the dilemma itself. For compatibilists, acting freely does not mean acting without causes; it means acting from one's own reasons and desires, without coercion or compulsion. On this account, a person who hands over a wallet at gunpoint acts less freely than one who donates the same money to charity, even if both actions are equally determined.

Neuroscience entered the argument in 1983, when Benjamin Libet and his colleagues reported that a pattern of brain activity known as the readiness potential began a fraction of a second before volunteers said they had become aware of deciding to move. Some commentators treated this as proof that the brain decides before the mind does. Later work has complicated that reading. In 2012, a team led by Aaron Schurger proposed that the signal might reflect the build-up of random neural fluctuations rather than a hidden decision already taken.

Even a settled interpretation of such experiments would leave much unresolved. Pressing a button at a moment of one's own choosing is far removed from deciding whom to marry or whether to break a promise, and it is precisely in those deliberate choices that questions of responsibility matter most.

sources.claim: Özgür irade tartışmasında belirlenimcilik, liberteryenlik (özgür iradenin belirlenimcilikle bağdaşmadığını ve özgür olduğumuzu savunan görüş) ve özgür irade şüpheciliği (özgür olduğumuzu reddeden görüş) başlıca tutumlardır.
sources.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Free Will; https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/freewill/

sources.claim: Bağdaşırcılık özgür iradenin belirlenimcilikle bağdaştığını savunur; özgürlüğü zorlama ya da kompulsiyon olmaksızın kişinin kendi gerekçeleriyle davranması olarak ele alır.
Libet ve meslektaşları 1983'te hazırlık potansiyelinin, katılımcıların hareket etme niyetinin farkına vardıklarını bildirdikleri andan saniyenin bir kesri kadar önce başladığını raporladı.
sources.source: Libet B, Gleason CA, Wright EW, Pearl DK (1983), Time of conscious intention to act in relation to onset of cerebral activity (readiness-potential), Brain 106(3): 623-642; https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/106.3.623

sources.claim: Schurger, Sitt ve Dehaene 2012'de hazırlık potansiyelinin kendiliğinden sinirsel dalgalanmaların birikimini yansıtabileceğini öne süren bir model önerdi.
sources.source: Schurger A, Sitt JD, Dehaene S (2012), An accumulator model for spontaneous neural activity prior to self-initiated movement, PNAS 109(42): E2904-E2913; https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1210467109
